info.title: Ownkube CLI API
info.description: API for the Ownkube CLI tool. Authenticate via browser-based flow, then use x-api-key header for subsequent requests.

organizations.description: Organizations this user belongs to. Pass an `id` as the `x-ownkube-organization` header on subsequent requests when membership is plural.

quickCreateUrl.description: Open in a browser and click Create stack (handoff mode)

AwsConnectTemplate.description: Deploy this stack yourself with AWS creds already in your environment (autonomous mode). Parameter keys match the template exactly.

awsAccountId.description: 12-digit AWS account ID once the stack reports in

status.description: pending (waiting on the stack) / configuring (provisioning access) / verified / failed

code.description: Raw CloudFormation status code this maps from

kind.description: How to recover: `retry` (transient/propagation, re-verify or re-launch the same stack), `quota` (fix an AWS limit then re-verify), `conflict` (account claimed elsewhere, use a different account).

description.description: What happened and what to do next

AwsConnectionFailure.description: Structured failure + remediation when status is `failed`

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: API key issued by the browser-based CLI authorization flow.

get.description: Returns the profile of the user associated with the provided API key.

get.summary: List organizations the API key's user belongs to
get.description: Use the returned `id` as the `x-ownkube-organization` header on subsequent requests when your account belongs to more than one org.

post.description: Mints a cross-account access request and returns the CloudFormation artifacts. Reuses this org's in-flight (unproven) row, so repeated calls do not pile up records. Poll GET /v1/aws/accounts/{accountId} until status is `verified` or `failed`.

delete.description: Blocked while any cluster still references the account (the cross-account role is required to tear infra down). Destroy those clusters first.

post.description: Normally the stack's phone-home finalizes the connection automatically. Call this to force a verify, optionally passing `awsAccountId` to assume the role directly before the callback arrives.

schema.description: 12-digit AWS account ID. Supply it to verify immediately (autonomous mode) instead of waiting for the stack's phone-home.

parameters.description: 12-digit AWS account ID. Supply it to verify immediately (autonomous mode) instead of waiting for the stack's phone-home.
parameters.name: awsAccountId

post.summary: Re-arm an account whose access stack was removed
post.description: Re-arms the existing row in place (same external ID and account ID) and returns a fresh CloudFormation link. Re-running the stack recreates the role and re-verifies the same account — no duplicate is created.

post.summary: Re-run account setup on a verified account
post.description: Re-applies the shared roles and policies for an already-verified account. Safe to call to pick up an available upgrade (`needsUpgrade: true`).

get.summary: List clusters in the current organization
List environments in the current organization
get.description: Default `Development` and `Production` environments are auto-seeded for orgs that have none yet, so this endpoint always returns at least two rows.

get.summary: List deployments by environment or cluster
get.description: Pass `environmentId` to scope to one environment, or `clusterId` to scope to one cluster. Exactly one is required.
Reads log lines from the in-cluster logs backend over the requested window. `filter` accepts a LogsQL regex matched against the message body.
Returns the host, port, credentials, and connection URI for a database deployment. Only valid for `resourceType: database`.

get.summary: List revisions for a deployment (newest first)
